entries.title: Two factors of two in the doubling iteration
entries.summary: The corrected iteration loses a factor of two in the exponent at a fixed length; the verified common Lieb–Robinson parameters recover the exact printed entropy bound.
entries.context: The main theorem is proved by contradiction: the largest entropy Sl of an interval of length l in a long window satisfies a strict doubling inequality, and iterating it from a starting length ξ0 = 2ξ′ ln(2C1) forces the entropy per site below zero after finitely many doublings.
entries.claims: Each doubling lowers the entropy per site Sl/l by 1/ξ′, and the contradiction bounds the window length l0 by ξ′ ln(2C1) times a power of two, giving the factor 2ξ′ ln D in Smax.
entries.found: Dividing the doubling inequality by 2l lowers Sl/l by 1/(2ξ′) per doubling, so twice as many doublings are needed; and the printed prefactor ξ′ ln(2C1) is ξ0/2, while the contradiction only gives l0 < ξ0 times the power of two. Three facts used implicitly (2C1 > 1, ln C1 + C2 ≥ 0, and the inequality only where both intervals fit in the window) are stated as hypotheses; none restricts the theorem.
entries.impact: At the original fixed length the corrected argument gives 4 raised to ξ′ ln D. With the admissible pair (v, ξ<sub>C</sub>) = (40c<sub>R</sub>J, 80), set s = max(80c<sub>R</sub>J/ΔE, 80) and ξ′ = 6s. The bound is then c<sub>0</sub> ξ′ ln ξ′ ln D · 2<sup>ξ′ ln D</sup>, with c<sub>0</sub> depending only on the interaction range.
entries.plan: The fixed-length correction and the printed-form comparison at the common source length have passed local proof and source verification. The new comparison is submitted for review and remains unmerged; earlier pieces of the doubling argument are merged.

entries.title: Constants of the mutual-information bound
entries.summary: The measurement uses the positive window effect O<sub>B</sub><sup>†</sup>O<sub>B</sub>; rescaling the error preserves its exponential rate and gives the explicit numerical constant 7.
entries.context: The entropy gain compares the ground-state marginal on a window with the product of its two marginals. Its two-outcome measurement uses the window effect E = O<sub>B</sub><sup>†</sup>O<sub>B</sub>. The product Q = O<sub>L</sub>O<sub>R</sub> of the two half-chain projections is an auxiliary operator.
entries.claims: The original argument uses O<sub>B</sub> as a positive effect and y = Tr(Qσ) ≥ 1 − 2ε for the product state σ. The note added observes that O<sub>B</sub> need not be positive and instead uses E.
entries.found: The projections give y ≥ 1 − 2ε², so the printed linear lower bound on y holds for 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1. The ground-state expectation of E is at least 1 − 4ε. Under the bootstrap premise Tr(P<sub>0</sub>σ) ≤ 2ε, its product-state expectation is at most 20ε for ε ≤ 1/136. With η = 2ε, the binary relative-entropy argument gives the stated entropy gain with C<sub>2</sub> = 7 and prefactor 2C<sub>1</sub>.
entries.impact: The exponential rate is unchanged. This measurement argument does not incur the square-root loss needed to make the factorization itself positive.
entries.plan: The effect estimates and their relative-entropy consequence are proved, and are used under the high-entropy premise in the proof of the area law for gapped chains.

entries.result: Matrix product states, decay of the Schmidt tail
entries.title: Constant and sign in the decay of the Schmidt tail
entries.summary: The argument stands; the constant in the power-law decay of the Schmidt weight is e<sup>2/ξ′</sup> instead of e<sup>1/ξ′</sup>, and a missing minus sign in the exponent is restored.
entries.context: The matrix product state approximation needs the weight of the ground state beyond its first k′ Schmidt coefficients across a cut. The bootstrap gives it at the numbers k0D2m; interpolating between them gives a power law in k′.
entries.claims: The weight beyond k′ is at most 4C12 e1/ξ′ (k′/k0)1/(ξ′ ln D).
entries.found: The constraint holds only at even powers D2m, so when the integer part of logD(k′/k0) is odd one more factor e1/ξ′ is lost; and the exponent must be negative for the bound to decay.
entries.impact: No. The decay is the same power law with a slightly larger constant.
entries.plan: The corrected tail estimate and its Hamiltonian-level matrix product state consequence are proved, using the endpoint factorization at every cut.

entries.result: Lemma 1, the Gaussian filter and decay constants
entries.title: Gaussian filtering and the endpoint decay rate
entries.summary: Doubling the Gaussian parameter and enlarging an admissible Lieb–Robinson length gives the endpoint rate with a polynomial prefactor.
entries.context: The approximate ground-state projector is constructed by averaging time evolution against a Gaussian of variance q/ΔE², where ΔE is the gap. Its error is then bounded as the window length l grows.
entries.claims: The paper chooses q = lΔE/(6v), asserts a filtered-vector error of order e<sup>−l/(3ξ)</sup>, and states a final bound C<sub>1</sub>(ξ)e<sup>−l/(6ξ)</sup> with C<sub>1</sub> polynomial in ξ.
entries.found: The suppression is exp(−q/2), so doubling the printed q restores the intermediate rate. At a fixed length the final estimate retains a square-root prefactor and gives only strictly slower exponential rates. An auxiliary enlarged length ζ gives a contraction bound Kζ³ exp(−l/(6ζ)). The common pair (40c<sub>R</sub>J, 80) has source length s ≥ 2ζ, so both contraction and positive semidefinite factorizations satisfy Ks³ exp(−l/(6s)).
entries.impact: The printed Gaussian intermediate estimate needs correction. The corrected factorization reaches the stated endpoint form after choosing an enlarged admissible length, uniformly in chain length and local dimension.
entries.plan: The Gaussian correction is already proved. The interaction-proportional source pair and both common-length factorization statements have also passed local verification and are submitted for review and remain unmerged.

entries.result: Lemma 1, positivity of the window factor
entries.title: Positive factors and the square-root loss
entries.summary: The repair is positive semidefinite and halves the rate at a fixed length; enlarging the admissible source length restores the stated rate for positive factors as well.
entries.context: The left and right factors of the approximate projector are orthogonal projections. The middle factor B acts on the window and need not be positive.
entries.claims: The printed lemma asks for all three factors to be positive with error ε(l) = C<sub>1</sub>e<sup>−l/ξ′</sup>.
entries.found: The note added replaces B by B†B. Lemma 4 bounds the repaired error by √(1 − (1 − ε)²) + 3ε + ε² for small ε, giving a bound of order √ε and decay e<sup>−l/(2ξ′)</sup>. The constructed factors are positive semidefinite and can have kernels; the construction does not establish positive definiteness.
entries.impact: The positive-factor estimate has the slower rate at a fixed auxiliary length ζ. For the common source length s ≥ 2ζ it instead has error Ks³ exp(−l/(6s)), just as the contraction estimate. The correlation lemma therefore uses the same ξ′ = 6s as the area law and matrix product state approximation.
entries.plan: The Hermitian repair is merged. Its common-source-length application and the correlation consequence have passed local verification and are submitted for review and remain unmerged.

entries.result: Matrix product states, the approximation error
entries.title: The approximation error is a squared norm
entries.summary: The stated power law bounds squared Hilbert-space error of an unnormalized matrix product vector.
entries.context: Truncating the Schmidt decomposition at every internal cut gives a vector Φ, which need not have norm one. Let τ<sub>j</sub> be the discarded Schmidt weight at cut j.
entries.claims: The paper calls N(k′/k<sub>0</sub>)<sup>−1/(ξ′ ln D)</sup> an approximation error without specifying the norm convention.
entries.found: The proved estimate is ‖Φ − Ψ<sub>0</sub>‖² ≤ ∑<sub>j=1</sub><sup>N−1</sup>τ<sub>j</sub>. Consequently the unsquared norm has order √N(k′/k<sub>0</sub>)<sup>−1/(2ξ′ ln D)</sup>.
entries.impact: Polynomial bond dimension still gives polynomial accuracy for fixed chain parameters; interpreting the displayed rate as an unsquared norm would assert a stronger bound.
entries.plan: The squared-norm estimate is proved. Keep the norm and normalization conventions explicit when using it.

entries.result: Lemma 1, the commutator of a Hamiltonian part
entries.title: A factor in the boundary commutator bound
entries.summary: The printed commutator constant is too small; a range-dependent constant replaces it.
entries.context: The proof splits H into left, buffer and right parts. Its Gaussian estimate uses the norm of [H,H<sub>L</sub>].
entries.found: Two overlapping Pauli terms of norm one give commutator norm two. Counting the interacting terms gives a valid constant depending only on the interaction range, multiplied by J².
entries.impact: This changes a prefactor, not the form of exponential decay.
entries.plan: The corrected boundary commutator estimate is proved and is used in the filtered-part construction.

entries.result: Lemma 1, localization of the filtered parts
entries.title: Compare with the filtered Hamiltonian part
entries.summary: The localized operator approximates the Gaussian-filtered part, not the unfiltered part.
entries.context: A Hamiltonian part W is Gaussian averaged to W̃ and then replaced by a localized operator M. The increment M − W acts near the boundary.
entries.claims: The printed estimate makes ‖M − W‖ exponentially small.
entries.found: The required small quantity is ‖M − W̃‖. The local increment M − W need not be small. Conditional expectation and the Duhamel formula give the corrected estimate in terms of ‖[H,W]‖.
entries.impact: The corrected quantity is exactly the one needed to transfer the small ground-state residual of W̃ to M.
entries.plan: The corrected localization estimate is proved and used in Lemma 1. The former identification problem for the Lieb–Robinson parameters has now been discharged in the locally verified common-source-length theorem.

entries.title: Use an absolute spectral threshold
entries.summary: The cutoff must keep eigenvalues of small absolute value, not all eigenvalues below a positive threshold.
entries.context: The localized Hermitian parts M<sub>L</sub>, M<sub>R</sub> have ground-state expectation zero and need not be positive. Their cutoffs define the left and right projections.
entries.claims: The source keeps eigenvalues λ ≤ θ and later uses ‖MO‖ ≤ θ.
entries.found: A negative eigenvalue below −θ violates that norm bound. Keeping |λ| ≤ θ gives both ‖MO‖ ≤ θ and ‖(1 − O)Ψ‖ ≤ ‖MΨ‖/θ.
entries.impact: The correction justifies the subsequent cutoff estimates without changing their constants.
entries.plan: The absolute-threshold bounds are proved and used in the construction.

entries.title: A common Lieb–Robinson pair for every consequence
entries.summary: A numerical finite-support bound proves the common pair (40c<sub>R</sub>J, 80), so all factorization, entropy, approximation and correlation statements use the source length ξ′ = 6s.
entries.context: The source sets ξ = max(2v/ΔE, ξ<sub>C</sub>) from a Lieb–Robinson estimate with numerical prefactor, velocity proportional to the interaction strength J, and a numerical decay length ξ<sub>C</sub>. Its second observable may act on any finite support. These same parameters must enter the later lemmas and the main theorem.
entries.claims: The source requires a controlled prefactor, velocity v of order J, length ξ<sub>C</sub> of order one, and a factorization constant polynomial in ξ.
entries.found: The chain commutator estimate has numerical prefactor 4 times the first-support size and no second-support cardinality factor. Its time-cone form holds for every positive v ≥ 8c<sub>R</sub>J and ξ<sub>C</sub> ≥ 8. Taking (v, ξ<sub>C</sub>) = (40c<sub>R</sub>J, 80) gives s = max(80c<sub>R</sub>J/ΔE, 80). The positive factorization, bootstrap and Rényi bounds, mutual-information step, printed entropy bound, matrix product state threshold and correlation lemma all use ξ′ = 6s.
entries.impact: The former restriction on matching the source parameters is removed. The gap-dependent auxiliary velocities remain valid intermediate estimates, while the final common velocity is proportional to J. The reciprocal-length convention and the fixed-length corrections remain explicit.
entries.plan: All common-parameter statements have passed the full local build, strict checks, standard-axiom and blueprint declaration checks, and mathematical source review. They are submitted for review and remain unmerged.

entries.result: Matrix product states, the Hamiltonian application
entries.title: The conditional entropy premise and the Hamiltonian application
entries.summary: The Hamiltonian supplies both premises at the common source length: the printed entropy bound fixes a chain-length-independent truncation threshold, and the factorization controls the discarded Schmidt weight.
entries.context: The source’s matrix product state section explicitly assumes a uniform entropy bound. A common integer k<sub>0</sub> ≥ exp(2S<sub>j</sub>)/2 at every internal cut turns its cut-dependent real threshold into a single truncation parameter.
entries.claims: For ground states of gapped chains, the preceding area law and factorization provide constants uniform in the cut and chain length.
entries.found: The conditional theorem takes the entropy and factorization bounds as hypotheses, just as the paper's construction does, and gives an unnormalized matrix product vector Φ. For N < 2, Φ = Ψ<sub>0</sub>; for N ≥ 2, ‖Φ − Ψ<sub>0</sub>‖² ≤ (N − 1)4C<sub>1</sub>²e<sup>2/ξ′</sup>(k′/k<sub>0</sub>)<sup>−1/(ξ′ ln D)</sup>, with k′ ≥ k<sub>0</sub>. For a gapped chain the area law supplies k<sub>0</sub> = ⌈exp(2S<sub>max</sub>)/2⌉ and Lemma 1 supplies the factorization, both independent of the chain length. The source-length theorem uses ξ′ = 6s and the printed S<sub>max</sub> = c<sub>0</sub> ξ′ ln ξ′ ln D · 2<sup>ξ′ ln D</sup>.
entries.impact: The conditional entropy premise is discharged from the Hamiltonian, and no restriction on matching the source length remains. The squared-norm and normalization conventions remain explicit.
entries.plan: The conditional construction and earlier Hamiltonian applications are merged. The common-source-length application, with its threshold from the printed entropy maximum, has passed local verification and is submitted for review and remains unmerged.

entries.title: The orders of the Rényi bootstrap lemma
entries.summary: The Rényi form of the bootstrap lemma holds for every order the paper covers: orders below one by the paper's argument, orders above one by comparison with the von Neumann entropy.
entries.context: The Rényi entropy of order α is S<sub>α</sub>(ρ) = ln tr ρ<sup>α</sup>/(1 − α). At the end of the bootstrap lemma the paper remarks that the same Schmidt-tail constraints also bound S<sub>α</sub> of the half chain.
entries.claims: For sufficiently large α, maximizing the Rényi entropy under the tail constraints gives a series that converges whenever e<sup>−2α/ξ′</sup>(D<sup>2</sup>)<sup>1−α</sup> < 1, and the bound differs from the von Neumann bound only in the function replacing F(ξ′, D).
entries.found: The paper's maximization uses concavity of t ↦ t<sup>α</sup> and so covers 0 < α < 1 with the convergence condition, with 4 ln D − ln(1 − (D<sup>2</sup>)<sup>1−α</sup>e<sup>−2α/ξ′</sup>)/(1 − α) in place of F(ξ′, D). For α > 1, where the condition always holds, concavity of the logarithm gives S<sub>α</sub> ≤ S, so the von Neumann bound applies with F(ξ′, D) itself.
entries.impact: No. Every order is covered, so the restriction to orders below one is removed.
entries.plan: Both order ranges are already proved. Their common-source-length forms at ξ′ = 6s have passed local verification and are submitted for review and remain unmerged; they carry no inherited restriction on the Lieb–Robinson parameters.

entries.result: Cited result, constant bond dimension at one cut
entries.title: A constant bond dimension with different constants
entries.summary: Nothing is wrong with the cited paper. This note concerns a lemma of Landau, Vazirani and Vidick, listed here because they attribute it to Hastings' area law; the formalization proves a bond dimension of the same form as theirs, independent of the chain length and of the cut, but with constants taken from a different area-law argument, not Hastings' argument.
entries.context: Their polynomial-time algorithm for ground states of gapped chains needs, at every cut, a number B<sub>δ</sub> independent of the chain length such that keeping the B<sub>δ</sub> largest Schmidt vectors of the ground state Γ leaves a normalized vector of overlap at least 1 − δ with Γ. They quote this from Hastings' area law and its later sharpening, without proof.
entries.claims: B<sub>δ</sub> = exp(O(ε<sup>−1</sup> log<sup>3</sup> d log(1/δ))), for a chain of qudits of dimension d with gap ε and nearest-neighbour terms 0 ≤ H<sub>i</sub> ≤ 1.
entries.found: The formalization proves the statement for every δ > 0 and every cut from the one-dimensional area law already in the library, not from Hastings' argument: B<sub>δ</sub> is the exponential of an affine function of log(1/δ), independent of the chain length and the cut, but with slope and intercept taken from that area law rather than the dependence ε<sup>−1</sup> log<sup>3</sup> d. A related counting factor in their size-trimming step becomes (D + 1)D in place of D.
entries.impact: None for the existence statements, and none for Hastings' theorems: nothing else on this page depends on this lemma. Their later steps use only that B<sub>δ</sub> is independent of the chain length and the cut, so the different constant changes the explicit running time, not the conclusions.
entries.plan: Derive their dependence on ε<sup>−1</sup> log<sup>3</sup> d from the sharper area law of Arad, Kitaev, Landau and Vazirani if the explicit running time is ever wanted; that work is followed on the tab for ground states in polynomial time.
